comments.body:
**Resolution: solution written from scratch (no prior solution.tex existed).**

**Answer: No.** The only irreducible (local) finite $k$-scheme that is rigid is $\operatorname{Spec}(k)$. Equivalently, every finite-dimensional local commutative $k$-algebra $A\neq k$ has $T^1_A\neq 0$.

**Proof outline (full details in solution.tex):**

1. *Presentation.* Write $A=R/I$ with $R=k[x_1,\dots,x_n]_{(x)}$ regular local, $n=\dim_k\mathfrak m/\mathfrak m^2$ the embedding dimension, the $x_i$ mapping to a basis of $\mathfrak m/\mathfrak m^2$. Then $I\subseteq\mathfrak m_R^2$ (Lemma 1) and $I\neq0$ (else $A\cong R$, impossible by finite-dimensionality).

2. *Lichtenbaum–Schlessinger model (characteristic-free).* $T^1_A\cong\operatorname{coker}\big(J:A^n\to\operatorname{Hom}_A(I/I^2,A)\big)$, $J(\theta)([f])=\sum_i\pi(\partial f/\partial x_i)\theta_i$ the dual Jacobian.

3. *Reduction mod $\mathfrak m$.* $\rho:\operatorname{Hom}_A(I/I^2,A)\to\operatorname{Hom}_A(I/I^2,k)\cong(I/\mathfrak m_R I)^*$, $\varphi\mapsto q\circ\varphi$, is **surjective** (explicit lift from a minimal generating set of $I$, with full well-definedness check).

4. *$\rho$ kills $\operatorname{im}(J)$.* Since $I\subseteq\mathfrak m_R^2$, every $\partial f/\partial x_i\in\mathfrak m_R$, so $J(\theta)([f])\in\mathfrak m$, hence $q\circ J(\theta)=0$.

5. So $\rho$ induces a surjection $T^1_A=\operatorname{coker}(J)\twoheadrightarrow(I/\mathfrak m_R I)^*$. By Nakayama $I\neq0\Rightarrow I/\mathfrak m_R I\neq0$, so the dual is nonzero and $T^1_A\neq0$. $\square$

**Explicit deformation.** For a minimal generating set $f_1,\dots,f_r$ of $I$, $A_\varepsilon=R[\varepsilon]/(\varepsilon^2,f_1-\varepsilon,f_2,\dots,f_r)$ is flat and nontrivial; e.g. $k[x]/(x^2)\rightsquigarrow k[x,\varepsilon]/(\varepsilon^2,x^2-\varepsilon)$.

**Verification.** Cross-checked symbolically against $A=k[x]/(x^2)$ ($T^1=k$, matching the Tjurina algebra; nonzero in char 2 too) and $A=k[x,y]/(x,y)^2$ ($T^1\twoheadrightarrow k^3$).
